findings.inspection_type: Analytic counterexample and exact finite enumeration
findings.title: Ensemble saturation does not bound gains from permitted unsubmitted methods
locations: Section8, PDFp.9, left column, second paragraph
findings.source_claim: Little or no improvement when ensembling submissions is used to infer that competitions extract near-maximal signal within constraints.
findings.suspect_step: Restriction to the information in submitted predictions is not an upper bound on all permitted hypotheses.

check.analytic_result: Submitted vector depends only onX1 and is independent ofY. Every deterministic prediction-only ensemble accuracy1/2; randomized mixtures remain1/2. g accuracy1.

alternative_readings: Authors' past empirical ensemble observation is not contradicted.
Large diverse participation can suggest broad search, but a separate coverage/optimality premise is required.
Adding rawX2 to a newly learned ensemble expands its information/hypothesis family.
No formal theorem or exhaustive hypothesis class is claimed in the paper; this is a failure of the stated supporting implication.
findings.supported_impact: Minor retained on the paper's dependency structure: the demonstrated damage is the unsupported reassurance about deadline opportunity cost. Its removal leaves that tradeoff open, while the proposed contemporaneous-comparison mechanism does not use search completeness as a premise. Survival of the general value of competitions, section placement, paper type and repair ease are not the rationale.

repair.statement: Limit the observation to tested combinations of submitted predictions; explicitly state that it does not bound gains outside that family.
repair.status: Logical repair supported by analytic proof and exact enumeration
repair.stronger_claim_requires: Defined permitted class and independent optimality/search-coverage evidence

findings.version_status: Persists in frozen/current publisher PDF and normalized-text-identical arXivv2; no labeled erratum located

severity_calibration.core_dependency: The failed inference supplies the response to the objection that a fixed deadline excludes valuable submissions. A deadline is constitutive of the proposed design, so the objection is substantive. However, Section1.1 grounds the gold-standard rationale in anti-cheating practices and renewable tasks; Sections6.1-6.2 describe contemporaneous comparisons and guarded/prospective test data; Section7 explicitly treats results as point-in-time evaluations. None requires submitted models to exhaust the permitted hypothesis class.
assumptions_rechecked: Common input access, equally simple permitted predictors and the same population-accuracy objective
Every prediction-only map of the submitted outputs is covered by the saved exact check
Independent teams need not have independent errors or exhaustive hypothesis coverage
A newly learned rule using additional raw-feature information expands the family beyond the original submitted-prediction ensemble
counterevidence_and_survivors: If constraints mean all permitted predictors, the inference fails.
If constraints mean only submitted predictions, saturation may describe that family but cannot answer the excluded-submission objection.
The authors' historical small-gain observation remains unrefuted.
No method, metric, contamination-control mechanism or downstream recommendation is derived from near-optimality; Section7 explicitly avoids an immutable final conclusion.
